note: Friday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Thu 30 Jul US close. The tape SNAPPED BACK: the day after Wednesday's hawkish-hold selloff, US stocks staged a sharp relief rally — Nasdaq +2.8% to 25,122 (best day of the year, ending a six-day losing streak), S&P 500 +1.7% to a record 7,437.63, Dow +1.2% to 52,208 — led by Microsoft's record one-day market-value gain and a semiconductor rebound. After the close Amazon jumped ~9% AH (AWS +37%, capex raised to ~$220bn, re-validating AI spend) while Apple fell ~4% AH on a Services miss. Macro was 'stagflation-lite' — Q2 GDP slowed to +1.5%, June core PCE sticky at +3.3% y/y — keeping the Fed hawkish (10Y ~4.68%, 2Y fresh 2026 highs) even as the market looked through it. Gold pushed to ~$4,080 near a record; oil held >$92 Brent as the US-Iran pause stayed broken. Sentiment: CNN Fear&Greed printed ~32 ('Fear') on 30 Jul but that reading LAGS the intraday rebound; the dashboard fetches Fear&Greed LIVE in-browser (this baked value is the fallback). Breadth improved on the rally. Flows are LAGGED: the freshest BofA/EPFR Flow Show is still the week to 22 Jul (the week-to-29-Jul report releases ~Fri 31 Jul and is not yet out) — labeled as such; it pre-dates the 28-30 Jul round-trip. CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the composite and cited internals and labeled as such.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index rallied +1.7% to a record 7,437.63 on Thu 30 Jul, back above a rising 125-DMA after the one-day FOMC dip — momentum turned neutral-to-constructive on the rebound. [Inferred — CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Net new highs improved as the index reclaimed record ground on the +1.7% rally, though leadership remains concentrated in mega-cap tech — a neutral-to-mildly-fearful read. [Inferred from exchange data]

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). NYSE advancers led on the +1.7% rebound day, turning the daily breadth positive after two down days; the Summation Index is still recovering off its recent roll-over — improving but not yet decisively bullish. [Inferred — mcoscillator/Barchart JS-gated this run]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand had skewed heavily hedged through the FOMC risk-off; the 5-day average is still elevated (fearful) even as spot demand eased on the rally. [Inferred]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX eased from Wednesday's spike (~20.66) back toward ~18 on Thu 30 Jul as the relief rally took hold — a de-escalation from fear toward neutral. [VIX confirmed via Yahoo/Cboe]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Stocks rallied hard while Treasuries SOLD OFF (10Y rose ~10bp to ~4.68% on sticky 3.3% core PCE) — bonds gave no bid and money chased gold to a near-record; the 20-day stock-vs-bond spread stays fearful on the bond side. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS stayed historically tight (~277bp area, ~16th percentile) with only modest widening — credit shows no funding stress, the least-fearful gauge. [FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, ~277bp and edging wider]

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 200-day MA
metrics.value: ~mid-to-high 60s% (was ~68.6% on 16 Jul, the highest since February, and ~70% by 28 Jul per Seeking Alpha; the 28-29 Jul selloff eased it before Thursday's +1.7% rebound firmed it back into the mid-to-high 60s — a clean dated 30 Jul close was not retrievable as Barchart $SPXA200R is JS-gated). A majority above trend — a constructive longer-term backdrop. 52-wk range roughly 42-70

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
metrics.value: ~50-55% (had crossed >50% for the first time since February in late July per Seeking Alpha; the FOMC-day dip knocked it back but Thursday's broad +1.7% advance likely nudged it back to/above the 50% line) — short-term participation is borderline-to-improving. Approximate; clean 30 Jul value not retrievable

metrics.label: NYSE advancers vs decliners (latest session)
metrics.value: Advancers led on Thu 30 Jul as the broad market rallied +1.7% (directional; a clean NYSE-composite A/D count for the 30 Jul tape was not pullable from free sources this run) — positive breadth on the rebound day after two down days, with tech/semis and cyclicals leading the recovery

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: Turning up — the Oscillator swung positive on the broad rebound day after the two-day selloff pushed it negative; the Summation Index remains below its 8 May peak but is stabilizing. A confirmed dated numeric level was not retrievable from free sources this run (StockCharts $NYMO/$NYSI JS-gated). Direction improving

metrics.label: 52-week New Highs minus New Lows (NYSE)
metrics.value: Improving — the record index close on 30 Jul lifted new highs back above new lows after the selloff briefly flipped them negative; a precise NYSE-specific dated figure was not confirmed this run

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Recovering — the A-D line rolled over on the 28-29 Jul risk-off but turned back up with the broad +1.7% rebound and the record S&P close; the Nasdaq's +2.8% snapback and the semis recovery restored participation (inferred trend read)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: Estimated ~64-73% (roughly 7-8 of 11 sector ETFs) and firming — the broad rebound lifted tech/semis, discretionary and financials back above trend while Energy stays supported by the oil spike. A clean dated count was not extractable this run (inferred from the recovering index-level breadth)

breadth.note: Breadth firmed on Thursday's broad relief rally: longer-term participation stays a majority-above-trend (~mid-to-high 60s% of S&P members over their 200-DMA) and the shorter 50-DMA gauge nudged back toward/above the 50% line as advancers led and the record S&P/Nasdaq snapback restored semis leadership. The internals had rolled over on the 28-29 Jul FOMC selloff; the AWS/MSFT-led rebound (Nasdaq +2.8%, best day of the year) reversed most of that damage — broadening, recovering participation rather than a narrow melt-up. Several sub-metrics (exact 200-/50-DMA close, daily A/D, McClellan level, net new highs) were JS-gated or lagged this run and are labeled approximate. The open question: whether the 31 Jul Flow Show and next week's SGX/HK earnings confirm the risk-on turn or the sticky-inflation/hawkish-Fed backdrop re-caps it.

flows.period: BofA 'Flow Show' / EPFR week ending Wednesday 22 July 2026 (still the freshest verifiable weekly — the week-to-29-Jul report releases ~Friday 31 Jul and is NOT yet out at this run). These flows PRE-date the 28-30 Jul FOMC selloff-and-rebound round-trip, the oil spike and the chip rout/recovery; treat the risk-on EM/China tilt as a pre-shock snapshot. Weekly flows lag ~2-6 days. Labeled week-to-22-Jul 2026.
flows.narrative: The freshest weekly read (to 22 Jul, pre-turmoil) showed a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which posted its record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever (+$21.3bn) and drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record (+$29.6bn) on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn. Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn), gold (+$2.0bn, largest since April) and crypto (+$0.9bn) — a barbell chasing EM/China upside while hedging FOMC-hike and geopolitical risk. This snapshot pre-dates the hawkish hold, the Iran-pause breakdown AND Thursday's AWS/MSFT-led rebound, so the next Flow Show (to 29 Jul, out ~Friday) is the tell on whether the risk-on EM tilt survived the round-trip. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at an extreme 9.6 and the July FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian Cash-Rule SELL trigger, active since May) — stretched-bullish positioning that both amplified the Wednesday drop and fueled Thursday's snapback; the next FMS lands mid-August.

regions.note: US-domestic equity funds bled -$7.2bn (wk to 22 Jul) even as the aggregate global-equity number stayed positive — money left the US for EM/China. This pre-dates the 28-30 Jul round-trip; with FMS cash at just 3.6% (contrarian sell), the stretched-bullish positioning amplified both the hawkish-hold drop and Thursday's rebound.

The 2nd-largest weekly EM-equity inflow on record, China-fuelled — the marquee flow of the week and a bid under the HK-tech core into the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal. A pre-shock reading; watch whether it survives in the 31 Jul Flow Show.

China's record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever, on stronger-than-expected Politburo stimulus wording and the biggest MLF injection in five months — but southbound Stock Connect turned to OUTFLOWS on the chip rout later in the week (e.g. Xiaomi/SMIC net sold), a caution that the 31 Jul Flow Show may show fading.

A 7th consecutive week of Japan-equity inflows — the persistent DM haven within the rotation, on governance reform and BoJ normalization. (Korea separately +$1.5bn, a record +$16.3bn over four weeks.)
Europe joined the US on the outflow side as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex, with the UK outflow the largest since November.

A large money-market OUTFLOW — cash redeployed into equities, bonds and gold rather than hoarded. BofA's FMS cash level (3.6% of AUM) still trips the contrarian Cash-Rule sell signal; parked cash yields ~3.5-3.75% — the book's productive dry powder through the round-trip.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge that pre-dates the post-FOMC yield jump (10Y ~4.68%); HY OAS ~277bp signals no credit stress yet. IG/HY split not separately itemized this run.

The largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April, on the FOMC-hike/geopolitical hedge bid — and validated by spot pushing to ~$4,080 near a record through the FOMC round-trip. Gold's YTD inflow remains a record; BofA flags elevated net-longs. (Crypto funds +$0.9bn the same week.)
